issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for Girard's time in the library with Félix. It says only that he came back in at 10:46 and went up to Félix in the library, and it gives no departure time.
issues.misreading: A solver could read 'didn't stay long' as a short visit that ended soon after the 10:50-ish hall-clock reading, and use that to place Girard's departure or Félix's whereabouts at a time the sheet never states.

issues.quote: He had the brandy with him.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about who had brandy or where it was. It mentions only Girard's own brandy after dinner.
issues.misreading: A solver could take this as an extra whereabouts or circumstance for Félix in the library at the time of the visit, which the sheet does not give.

issues.quote: I'd barely got it going when the piano started up in the salon, just as I lit my cigar, at twenty-nine minutes past ten by my watch.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says the piano started just as Girard lit his cigar, at 10:29 by his watch, which makes the two events simultaneous.
issues.misreading: 'Barely got it going when' reads as the piano starting after the cigar was lit, which suggests a sequence rather than a simultaneous event. The clock reading is unchanged, so this is minor.
